extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating multimodal models on college-level, multi-discipline understanding and reasoning tasks. It contains 11.5K questions across six core disciplines, with heterogeneous image types and interleaved text-image inputs.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was manually curated in three stages: the authors first selected 30 subjects from six disciplines based on common university majors and the presence of visual inputs; then over 50 university students, including co-authors, collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources and created new questions where necessary; finally, the authors cleaned duplicates, checked format/typos, and assigned difficulty levels, excluding about 10% of overly easy problems.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with the design criteria, were excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions sourced from major textbooks and online resources, with some new questions created by annotators; the paper also describes the benchmark as drawing from online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The benchmark questions were manually collected by over 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in the relevant majors. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, and created new questions based on their expertise where necessary. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations and to avoid questions with immediately available answers. For quality control, authors removed duplicates, checked format and typos, and categorized difficulty levels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality control included duplicate detection using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, author review of suspected duplicates, format and typo checking, and difficulty categorization. The paper also reports an error analysis of 150 GPT-4V errors annotated by expert annotators, with error categories such as perceptual, lack of knowledge, reasoning, annotation, rejection, and answer extraction errors.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the relevant majors; additionally, 90 college senior students were used as human experts for validation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases, and GPT-4V often exhibits a bias towards perceptual errors.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU has limitations despite its comprehensive nature; the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. It also combines multiple-choice with concise open-ended questions to address challenges associated with evaluating open-ended responses.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: A benchmark for evaluating the capabilities of LMMs in the context of Expert AGI, assessing both basic perceptual skills and complex reasoning abilities across professional domains. Strong performance on this benchmark should be a necessary criterion for an Expert AGI system.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The benchmark was manually curated, with duplicate problems removed, typos/format issues corrected, and about 10% of very easy problems excluded from the final benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data were collected from textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials; then cleaned by deduplication, typo/format correction, and filtering out very easy problems not aligning with the benchmark design.

name.evidence: We introduce MMMU: a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks

description.evidence: MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines... These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types
